disclaimer: Educational reference only. Never eat any wild plant, berry, or fungus based on an app. Confirm with a qualified local expert.

universal_rules.text: No wild mushroom is ever confirmed by an app.

species.toxicity_mechanism: None when ripe and correctly identified; gastrointestinal upset if large quantities of unripe fruit eaten.
visual_prompts: Whole lowbush blueberry shrub with small oval leaves and clusters of round dusty-blue berries
Close-up of ripe round blue berries with crown-like calyx scar on blueberry bush
Detail of small oval finely toothed blueberry leaves turning red in autumn
Low spreading blueberry barrens growth habit with many stems
verification_checklist: Berries are round, dusty blue with a pale bloom
Calyx forms a five-pointed crown on the blossom end
Leaves are small, oval, finely toothed
Shrub is low and spreading, not a tall vine
Berries grow singly or in small clusters, not in elongated racemes
species.symptoms_if_ingested: None expected for ripe fruit; unripe fruit may cause mild stomach upset.
first_aid: Contact poison control if uncertain of identification.
species.notes: Scaffold entry; full database lands in Phase 4.

universal: Call your local emergency number if there is difficulty breathing, seizures, or loss of consciousness.
Do not induce vomiting unless instructed by poison control.
Photograph and bag a sample of what was eaten.
Note the time of ingestion and amount.

regions.label: United States
regions.note: Verify for your area; Canadian provinces use regional poison centres.
